Modules and type-only imports

7.0.2

Modules define which types and values other files can use.

Open interactive lesson

On this page

  • Keep type imports explicit
  • Match module settings to your runtime
  • Official references

Keep type imports explicit

Use import type for declarations that are only used in type positions. It is removed from the JavaScript output. Use a normal import for values you call or read at runtime.

// product.ts
export type Product = { name: string; price: number };
export const currency = "USD";

// label.ts
import { currency } from "./product.js";
import type { Product } from "./product.js";

export function label(item: Product) {
  return item.name + ": " + currency + " " + item.price;
}

Match module settings to your runtime

Use settings that match the environment loading your files. In a Node ESM project, relative paths to compiled files normally include the .js extension. A bundler can use different resolution rules, so use the settings recommended by your build tool.

// package.json: { "type": "module" }
// tsconfig.json: { "compilerOptions": { "module": "NodeNext" } }

// format.ts
export const formatLabel = (name: string) => name.toUpperCase();

// main.ts
// The import points to format.js in the compiled output.
import { formatLabel } from "./format.js";
console.log(formatLabel("Notebook"));
